verdictSummary: The loop that made Notability famous, ink plus an audio recording you can replay by tapping a stroke, is a small data model: timestamped points and an audio file. An agent can build a working PWA for it, PDF markup included. The gap is feel. Native Apple Pencil latency, prediction and smooth zoom on long notes are hard in a browser, and handwriting search, sync and the AI study tools are the parts Notability now charges for.
coreLoopDIY: A PWA where you write with Apple Pencil, record audio at the same time, tap a stroke to replay the audio from that moment, and mark up imported PDFs.
requirements: iPad with Safari, or a desktop browser
whatYouLose: native Pencil latency and stroke prediction
sync across iPad, iPhone and Mac
browser storage can be evicted, so backups are on you
moatNotes: native ink feel; years of class notes stuck in a proprietary format
whyPeopleStillPay: Students pay because the ink feels right and their whole degree already lives in it. Moving years of notes out is painful, and the free tier stops at 5 notes, so the habit converts into a subscription. The newer price is for AI transcription and study tools, which a weekend build will not match.

notes: The audio-synced ink is the buildable part; the subscription now sells AI study tools.
prompt:
Build a personal handwritten-notes app that replaces Notability, in an empty folder.
Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript PWA, perfect-freehand for ink, pdf.js for PDFs, Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage. No other stack.
It must run in Safari on iPad (installable to the home screen) and in desktop Chrome.
Core loop: open a notebook, write with Apple Pencil or a mouse, record audio while writing, then tap any stroke to replay the audio from that moment.
Canvas: pointer events with pressure, palm rejection (ignore touch while a pen is active), pen, highlighter, stroke eraser, lasso move, undo/redo, pages that scroll vertically.
Store every stroke as points with x, y, pressure and a timestamp relative to the recording start.
Audio: MediaRecorder, one or more recordings per note; playback mode highlights strokes as they were written.
PDF: import a PDF as page backgrounds and draw on top; export the annotated note back to PDF with pdf-lib.
Typed text boxes and pasted images on the page.
Library: notebooks and dividers, note titles, sort by date, search titles and typed text.
Templates: blank, lined, grid, dotted page backgrounds.
Backup: export and import the whole library as one .zip (JSON strokes + audio + PDFs). No account, no server.
Keep drawing at 60 fps on a 50-page note: render finished strokes to cached bitmaps, draw only the live stroke on a top layer.
Ask for microphone permission only when recording starts and explain why in the UI.
Out of scope, on purpose: cloud sync, handwriting-to-text, AI summaries, transcription, collaboration, native apps.
README: install, how to add to the iPad home screen, where data lives (IndexedDB, can be evicted, so back up), backup steps.
Write tests for stroke serialization, audio-time lookup for a tapped stroke and zip round-trip; run them and list the commands.
